title: AI search vendors hit federal-EU-state three-front regulatory anchor by H1 2027
body: Three regulatory fronts on AI search vendors crystallized inside a single 72-hour window, and by H1 2027 we expect the first federal motion-to-dismiss ruling on an AI-search copyright case (likely a Perplexity case given the active suit volume), the first EU AI Office enforcement action under the Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI, and the first DOJ amicus brief in a state-AI-labor-disclosure preemption case to all land — establishing the three-front contour every AI search vendor has to plan against. The trigger evidence is mechanical: CNN's May 28 copyright complaint in SDNY pushes Perplexity to nine active publisher suits, making a federal motion-to-dismiss ruling on at least one of those cases the near-term path to a first appellate-grade signal on AI-search-vs-copyright; OpenAI's same-day Frontier Governance Framework explicitly maps internal Preparedness Framework controls to the EU AI Act Code of Practice for GPAI and California Transparency in Frontier AI Act, putting the EU AI Office's August 2 2026 full-enforceability deadline on a now-named compliance scaffold that a first enforcement action can be measured against; and the DOJ federalism preemption thread against state AI labor disclosure statutes (with the May 14 Colorado SB 26-189 successor as the named recent state action) sets up a first amicus brief against a state AI-labor-disclosure law inside the federal-court calendar. The structural force is that the three obligations are non-transferable: a copyright settlement does not unlock EU AI Act compliance, an EU Code of Practice signing does not preempt state labor-disclosure rules, and a DOJ preemption win does not retire publisher copyright damages — so vendors cannot resolve them under a single compliance strategy and the cross-functional cost lands across legal, policy, and product simultaneously. The cross-sector landing pulls in courts (SDNY plus at least one EU member-state court if AI Office enforcement is contested), regulators (EU AI Office plus a US state attorney general), and standards bodies (the publisher-side cohorts that will follow the first SDNY ruling to anchor licensing-rate benchmarks), with Sam Altman's May 31 walk-back of his 2023 jobs-apocalypse rhetoric supplying the labor-impact axis a fresh public marker that state legislators will cite in successor disclosure statutes. The bear case is that the federal courts hold the first AI-search copyright case past H1 2027 on procedural grounds, the EU AI Office sequences enforcement toward general-purpose model providers before search agents, and the DOJ preemption brief slips into the FY28 docket — all three slipping would push the contour to late 2027; absent that triple slip, H1 2027 lands the first ruling, first enforcement action, and first amicus brief together as the named anchor every AI search vendor's GC and policy lead has to plan against.

reasoning.because: CNN suit pushes Perplexity to 9 publisher cases + EU Aug-2 GPAI deadline + DOJ state-preemption push
reasoning.given: OpenAI Frontier Governance maps to EU Code; Colorado SB 26-189; Altman labor walk-back
reasoning.so_that: First federal MTD ruling + first EU AI Office enforcement + first DOJ amicus brief in state-preemption case
reasoning.landing: By H1 2027; all three first-of-kind regulatory events land in one window
reasoning.plain_language: Three new fights — courts, EU, US states — over AI search will all reach big rulings together by mid-2027.

summary: CNN-vs-Perplexity pushes the publisher suit count to nine, OpenAI Frontier Governance maps to the EU Code of Practice ahead of Aug-2, and DOJ preemption follows Colorado SB 26-189. By H1 2027 the first federal MTD, first EU AI Office enforcement, and first DOJ amicus brief all land together.
